messages:
elyse: heads up — a customer hit a weird UX where their client keeps reconnecting every ~10s and the console shows nothing obvious. they see a bunch of quick 429s then a flood of reconnects.
raj: are those 429s from our gateway or the rate limiter service? any request ids?
miriam: gateway + quota. logs show short-lived 'throttle-window' spikes on the routing shard. sampling in the dashboard dropped the spike out of the aggregated view.
elyse: aha — so console telemetry smoothing is hiding the burst. users only see steady slot-level qps, not the short 10s surge that triggers client retries.
raj: that explains support tickets where they paste the console screenshot and we see nothing.
tom: can you paste the minimal log snippet? i want to confirm client behavior vs server-side backoff.
miriam: sure — snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T12:03:42Z] route=eu-west shard=shard-9 event=throttle window_ms=12000 token=opaque-abc id=req-7f9
[2026-03-10T12:03:44Z] route=eu-west shard=shard-9 event=reconnect client_id=svc-42 retries=1
[2026-03-10T12:03:52Z] route=eu-west shard=shard-9 event=throttle window_ms=10000 token=opaque-def id=req-8a1
```
elyse: client keeps trying, gets 429s, then SSE connection resets. because the console rollup uses 1m buckets + 1% sampling those 10s pulses vanish.
raj: two immediate asks: (1) add a short-term per-route spike counter metric we can surface in console (2) stop sampling throttle events by default (or sample differently)
miriam: i support (1). for (2) maybe make it an opt-in toggle under the streaming route page? defaulting off might cause noise for big tenants.
elyse: opt-in is fine but we need a first-class incident drill that maps "client reconnect storm" -> recent per-route throttle spikes. support currently has to jump to raw logs.
tom: operationally, i think we should emit a derived metric like streaming.throttle_spike{route,shard,region} with window=10s and threshold=5/s. that would be cheap (aggregate on the metrics side) and low-noise.
raj: metric name lgtm. we should also tag by routing_policy so customers who use latencypreference=fast can be correlated.
miriam: telemetry change approved. question: how do we surface it in console without blowing up charts? proposal: an overlay on the existing streaming dashboard: a small orange tickline for 10s spikes (toggleable legend).
elyse: +1. also add a tooltip that links to support playbook: "if you see repeated small spikes and client reconnects, check token rotation and route fallback".
deploy-bot: deploy request queued by miriam for branch: feature/spike-metric -> staging
tom: before staging, can we add a canary that only turns the overlay on for 10% of orgs and records if support tickets drop? we need a signal that visibility helps fix rate of tickets.
raj: canary is cheap. also update alerting: create a low-priority alert when streaming.throttle_spike > 10 across >= 3 shards in 30m — not P0 but useful.
miriam: added alert draft to ops-runbook, linking playbook and chart. will send PR for console overlay mockups in #design.
elyse: follow-ups: (A) add the metric emission + routing_policy tag (B) small console overlay toggle (C) run 10% canary and track support ticket rate over 2 weeks (D) doc the playbook for support.
tom: timeline? can we get metric + alert in 3 days, console mockups this week, canary next week?
miriam: i can push core metric + alert in 48h. console UX depends on design but i'll aim for a basic overlay next Wed.
raj: sgtm. once staging deploys, i'll validate with the affected customer's traffic replay.
elyse: thanks all — this should cut a lot of "why is nothing in metrics" tickets. :thumbsup:
raj: one more note — consider also exposing a per-connection "recent-retries" field in the tracing payload so we can tie a single client to repeated 429s in the console trace view.
miriam: nice idea, opening a follow-up issue for tracing enrichment.
elyse: logging action items in the thread: metric PR, alert PR, console toggle ticket, canary plan, tracing follow-up. i'll ping when PRs exist.
